title: Mindless Titan System
summary: Mindless Titan v3 is ImplementedDevelopment / 3.18.6 / Hybrid / ServerRigClientContactHints. PureTitanPredator retains responsive pursuit but now derives grounded approach and Backstep recovery from measured GroundFront palm reach instead of crowding the player under its root.
risks: PureTitanPredator difficulty 100 is the strongest-first Development baseline. v3.18.6 measures GroundFront central palm reach as `0.498618H`, approaches to `0.468701H`, and treats below `0.337465H` as too close. Valid-band targets are attacked without a behind-self destination; crowded Titans face the target and Backstep to authored spacing before GroundFront. Responsive turning and action-axis rules remain intact. The 42-scenario harness passes, but real owner collision/contact and 5/10/30 m expert-ODM acceptance remain open.

Replicated AI/F8 debug was removed after its response-tree tuple exceeded the unreliable-event payload limit. v3.18 also removes `ActionStarted` AI debug and simultaneous Shadow calculation. Exact planning is bounded to 3 ms or two solves per fixed step; six actions enter exact solving first and the search expands by two across later cognition ticks while pursuit continues. A fresh Play frame-time/clean-console rerun remains open because Studio MCP still did not transition out of Edit mode.

The single visible server rig removes client/proxy phase divergence; the 60 Hz anchored root step should reduce visible low-FPS/jitter, but Animator delivery and region-dependent smoothness still require two-real-client hands-on acceptance.
Visible palm contact remains a victim-client Tier-B hint. A malicious client can suppress hints to avoid grabs; server rig overlap without a hint is telemetry and never grants a hold.

The victim client owns the visible GrabVolume contact gate through action-scoped Touched signals plus an exact 60 Hz overlap fallback. Only direct character body parts count; the server keeps identity, action sequence, bounded timestamp, proximity, LOS, holder state, rate limits, and rewind checks. Real 30/60/120 FPS and 0-250 ms testing must confirm transient-contact reliability.

The 96-rig Development cap is provisional. Server frame, physics, replication bandwidth, client render, memory, Animator tracks, connections, welds, pool cleanup, and a 30-minute soak have not passed at cap.

Single-server rapid-release, historical-contact ownership, and miss-grace regressions pass. Two-client target-switch/action-lock, latency-dependent historical contact, grab rollback, observer hold, rescue, Blind release, full-clip Eat-to-Bite timing, moving-hook collision, nape/eye slash, 5 m/30 m collision, Death fade, and pool reuse remain open acceptance gates.

Automatic scale-aware body casts, persisted coarse waypoints, slope/ledge checks, and local replanning replace the authored-lane dependency, but wall, corridor, dynamic obstacle, and 5/10/30 m acceptance remain open.

Future-contact family planning, rear-axis commitment, per-target contextual miss isolation and success forgetting passed deterministic checks. The older SetupBrake, normal SetupCorrection, failure stand-off and lateral no-contact recovery motion paths are intentionally bypassed by v3.18.3 in favor of direct hunger pursuit; underfoot Backstep remains. Owner feel and all authored Capture families still require acceptance at 30/60/120 FPS and 0-250 ms latency.

The v3.2.7 Blind/Death server timeline passed preload, entry-weight, monotonic playback, and full-loop endpoint-freeze checks, but observer-client smoothness, region/network delivery, and unanchored expert ODM feel remain hands-on acceptance gates.
next: Owner-rerun stationary ground spacing and deliberate foot-level crowding first: confirm the Titan stops in authored GroundFront reach, attacks instead of watching, backs out while facing the player when below 0.337H, then grabs from the reopened angle; also confirm responsive orbit turning and real GrabVolume-only holds before broader gates.
